# Flow Free Solver

> A free, open-source Flow Free and Numberlink puzzle solver for desktop and mobile. Recreate or generate a board, connect matching dots, and fill every playable cell. All solving runs locally in the browser.

## Supported puzzles

- Classic / Numberlink, Classic with walls, Bridges, and Warps.
- Square and rectangular boards with 5 to 19 rows and columns.
- Blocks in every supported mode for missing corners, interior holes, and irregular shapes.
- Hexes and combined Bridges + Warps boards are not supported.

## How to use it

1. Choose a mode and board size; use Board options for rectangular dimensions.
2. Place two endpoints of each color and recreate any walls, blocks, bridges, or warp openings.
3. Select Solve to reveal a solution, or Edit to return to the puzzle.

## Solvers and limits

- Pruned DFS is the default: C compiled to WebAssembly, adapted from Matt Zucker's flow_solver, with independent diagonal edge searches inspired by Thomas Ahle's Numberlink. Open Classic boards retain their specialized fast path. Graph probes also handle walls, Blocks, independent bridge lanes, and warp seams. Variants permit self-touching paths and reject same-color crossings. Bounded or unsuccessful probes use the existing searches.
- Z3 SAT is the exact solver for Classic, walls, Bridges, and Warps on square or rectangular boards.
- A* is available for Classic square boards without walls.
- All available solvers support Blocks on their supported board types and run in Web Workers.
- Manually entered puzzles automatically try SAT if heuristic search reaches its limit. Puzzles may be unsolvable or time out.
- Generated puzzles retain a validated full-board solution. Generation does not check uniqueness or certify difficulty, and does not preserve custom walls or blocks.
- Puzzle boards are saved on the user's device.

## Documentation

- [Live solver](https://flow.kongesque.com/): Edit, generate, and solve puzzles in the browser.
- [README](https://github.com/Kongesque/flow-free-solver/blob/main/README.md): Supported modes, editor controls, algorithms, development, and licensing.
- [How the solver works](https://www.kongesque.com/blog/flow-free-solver): Technical explanation by the author.
- [Source code](https://github.com/Kongesque/flow-free-solver): React, TypeScript, Vite, and WebAssembly implementation.
- [Author](https://www.kongesque.com/): Kongesque.
